title: In situ particle-to-fibre transformation of hydrogels for 3D printing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC flags show no open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no data or database cross-references, and no text-mined accessions; NCBI links empty. No dataset size or structure is described.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use printing settings and particle/gel composition to predict the width and alignment of the hydrogel fibres produced.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one print condition (flow rate, nozzle size, particle and matrix recipe); number of examples unknown, no data found.
plain_idea.predict: Fibre diameter and alignment measured by microscopy in the paper's experiments.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Biofabrication labs could choose printing settings without trial-and-error, but only if hundreds of measured conditions existed, which this paper does not appear to provide.
